unreleased: The payment gateway can now ask Stripe's checkout for the payer's billing address and keeps the country Stripe reports with the payment (payment.extra["customer_country"], an upper-case ISO code, already visible to the purpose's on_paid hook) - the basis for VAT place of supply, OSS limits and local taxes. It is opt-in per payment (PaymentQuote.require_billing_address); a purpose that does not set it changes nothing.

Add a tickets module (app/modules/tickets), a ticketing system for administrators only (User.is_admin) that stands on its own and extends the contact form and the CRM when they are enabled: a ticket (numbered from 100001, type Issue / Order / General (the default) / Internal, open or closed) has a thread of internal notes, received messages and e-mails sent to the requester, each entry with the time spent on it (summed in the ticket's header), rich-text content with pictures, and private file attachments (pictures inside the text are served from an unguessable public address so the requester's mail client can show them). Tickets come from three sources: typed in by an administrator (optionally linked to a CRM partner), read every TICKETS_POLL_SECONDS from an IMAP mailbox configured in .env (TICKETS_IMAP_*; a new mail opens a ticket and, with the CRM on, is linked to the partner with the sender's address, otherwise to none), and the contact form - with the module enabled, a message also opens a ticket. Every mail about a ticket carries its number in the subject as "[Ticket#100253] - ..." and Reply-To is the mailbox, so an answer that keeps the number is added to that ticket (and reopens it) instead of opening a new one; mail from our own addresses and automatic mail that names no ticket never opens a ticket, and a mail read twice is filed once. The module manifest can now declare hooks (a module takes part in a flow another module owns, called only while it is enabled; the contact form's "contact_form.received" is the first) and background_tasks (started with the application, cancelled on shutdown; the mailbox poller is the first), and send_email takes reply_to, attachments and headers
Add app/services/sql.py with like_pattern(), the escaping of `%`, `_` and the escape character for a "contains" search, shared by modules instead of copied into each (the CRM module uses it now)

Add an event_booking module (app/modules/event_booking) for registering for an event, built on the event calendar and forms: a registration belongs to one event and offers slots made from blocks of days (a list of days, weekdays within a range, or any future day) and times (all day, a list, or generated every N minutes) with a capacity per slot - per day for an all-day slot; nothing is stored per slot, they are computed. A visitor books with name, e-mail, consent to the processing of personal data and the form's answers; who may book is public, signed-in only, or by a secret link (a registration reached by link is not mentioned to anyone without it). The capacity is checked under a lock on the registration row, so two people cannot take the last place, and registering is possible only while the registration is open, the article is published and the event is not over. A honeypot field and a limit of upcoming bookings per e-mail address slow spam down (there is no rate limiting). The person gets a confirmation with a link to cancel (a button on a page, never a GET) and the administrator a notice; administrators manage registrations and bookings, can move a booking, correct its name, e-mail and answers or cancel it with a note and an e-mail to the person (in the language they booked in, whose failure is reported and never undoes the change), see the history of changes, export a CSV (formula-safe) and a summary of the answers of confirmed bookings. Bookings are deleted a configurable number of months after their date (default 12), by a purge that runs at most once a day when a booking is made or the list is opened, or on demand. Texts and switches are in backend/modules/event_booking.json, the notice address in BOOKING_NOTIFY_MAIL (else CONTACT_MAIL); tzdata is now a dependency (local times are Europe/Prague)

Add a forms module (app/modules/forms) for other modules to build on: forms with questions of seven types (checkbox, radio, text, number, date, time, date and time), questions shown only when earlier answers say so (several conditions, chaining through hidden questions), validation of the answers on the server with error codes (the regular expression of a text question is run with a time limit, and one that backtracks catastrophically is refused when the form is saved), answers stored as a snapshot of the questions as they were worded when answered, and, for administrators, browsing the answers and a basic summary per question (counts and shares of the options, minimum / maximum / average / median of numbers, earliest and latest dates). The questions of a form are replaced as a whole list, in order; a form that still has answers cannot be deleted

The event calendar module now builds on articles: an event is just a date (or a run of days, with optional times, a title and a description of up to 128 characters) belonging to exactly one article, an article can have several. The wall (/dashboard) is made of articles - the one with the nearest upcoming date, the pinned ones and the last five past ones - the calendar, archive and search follow the article's visibility (archived articles stay findable), and search also looks through the article text ignoring diacritics. GET /by-article/{id} lists an article's dates. Events no longer have their own page, slug, image, status or pinned flag, and image upload moved to the articles module. The database table is recreated: existing events are NOT carried over

Add an articles module (app/modules/articles): articles with a title, perex, sanitized HTML content, image, status (draft / published / archived), optional display window, a pinned flag and a type, plus dynamic article types with frame and background colours for the light and dark theme. Public listing, search ignoring case and diacritics over title, perex and full text (archived articles included, drafts never), detail by slug, and administrator-only management with image upload; a type in use is deleted only with a replacement type

The shared HTML sanitizer now also keeps tables, text alignment, horizontal rules, code blocks and YouTube / Vimeo video embeds; frames from any other address, and anything that could run script, are still removed on every save

A module can declare the modules it requires (`ModuleManifest.requires`); enabling one without them now logs a warning at startup, naming both, instead of failing later in some request. The warning never stops the application

Add a portfolio module (app/modules/portfolio): projects with a Czech and an English title, short description and text, a link, a status (live or in preparation), tags and a publish flag, kept in an order the administrator sets. GET /api/modules/portfolio/items and /items/{slug} serve the published ones in the visitor's language, falling back to the other language when a text is missing; administrators manage them, reorder them and publish or hide them under /manage. The migration adds the table and seeds five projects

Add the freelancer module with GET /api/modules/freelancer/provider, which gives the legal pages the provider's details from PROVIDER_* in .env (name, company ID, address, registration, email, phone, effective date) and says whether the minimum is filled in

Switch on the contact-form module for this site, with its page heading, introduction and note, the address that receives messages shown as a contact detail, and the confirmation email written in the first person

Contact-form module: GET /api/modules/kontaktni_formular/info serves a per-language page heading, introduction and note (the new `page` block of backend/modules/kontaktni_formular.json) plus public contact details - address, GitHub and LinkedIn links from CONTACT_ADDRESS / CONTACT_GITHUB_URL / CONTACT_LINKEDIN_URL in .env, and the delivery address only when `show_email` is on. Nothing is shown until it is configured
Switch on the CRM module for this site: its partner, task and invoice endpoints are mounted under /api/modules/crm and open to administrators only

Add a CRM module (app/modules/crm), for administrators only: partners with contact and company details, their tasks (status, price, dates), and invoice PDFs uploaded against a task - checked to really be PDFs and capped at 10 MB, stored privately under uploads/crm/ and served only to administrators through an authenticated download
